SELECT o.work_centre, substr(o.completed_on,1,7) ym, COUNT(*) n_ops, ROUND(SUM(a.act)/SUM(o.est_setup_hours+o.est_run_hours),3) act_over_est
FROM erp_job_operations o JOIN a USING(op_id) WHERE substr(o.completed_on,1,7) IN ('2016-01','2016-02','2016-03','2016-06','2016-09','2016-12','2017-06') AND o.work_centre IN ('laser','paint','brake','mill')

WITH tc AS (SELECT CAST(substr(week_of,1,4) AS INT) yr, employee_id, SUM(regular_hours+overtime_hours) paid, COUNT(*) wks FROM hr_timecards GROUP BY 1,2),
lb AS (SELECT CAST(substr(work_date,1,4) AS INT) yr, employee_id, SUM(hours) clk FROM shop_labour_entries GROUP BY 1,2),
r AS (SELECT e.role, tc.yr, SUM(paid) paid, SUM(COALESCE(clk,0)) clk, SUM(wks) wks FROM tc LEFT JOIN lb USING(yr,employee_id) JOIN hr_employees e USING(employee_id) WHERE tc.yr BETWEEN 2016 AND 2025 GROUP BY 1,2),
rate AS (SELECT employee_id, arg_max(hourly, effective_on) hourly FROM hr_pay_rates WHERE effective_on <= '2025-12-31' GROUP BY 1),
rr AS (SELECT e.role, median(rate.hourly) med_rate FROM rate JOIN hr_employees e USING(employee_id) WHERE employee_id IN (SELECT employee_id FROM tc WHERE yr=2025) GROUP BY 1),
x AS (SELECT role,
 SUM(CASE WHEN yr=2025 THEN paid-clk END)-SUM(CASE WHEN yr=2016 THEN paid-clk END) d16,
 SUM(CASE WHEN yr=2025 THEN paid-clk END)-SUM(CASE WHEN yr=2017 THEN paid-clk END) d17,
 (SUM(CASE WHEN yr BETWEEN 2023 AND 2025 THEN paid-clk END)-SUM(CASE WHEN yr BETWEEN 2017 AND 2019 THEN paid-clk END))/3.0 d3avg,
 SUM(CASE WHEN yr=2017 THEN wks END) wks17, SUM(CASE WHEN yr=2025 THEN wks END) wks25,
 SUM(CASE WHEN yr=2016 THEN wks END) wks16
 FROM r GROUP BY 1)
SELECT role, ROUND(d16,0) d16, ROUND(d17,0) d17, ROUND(d3avg,0) d3avg, wks16, wks17, wks25, ROUND(med_rate,2) rate,
 ROUND(d17*med_rate,0) usd17, ROUND(d3avg*med_rate,0) usd3avg,
 ROUND(SUM(d16) OVER(),0) t16, ROUND(SUM(d17) OVER(),0) t17, ROUND(SUM(d3avg) OVER(),0) t3,
 ROUND(SUM(d17*med_rate) OVER(),0) tusd17, ROUND(SUM(d3avg*med_rate) OVER(),0) tusd3
FROM x JOIN rr USING(role) ORDER BY role

content.text:
I've saved `challenge.json`. My verdict on F9 is **stands with changes**: the pattern is real, but its size is overstated and part of the explanation doesn't hold up.

**What survived:**
- **Machining:** mill and lathe estimated workload fell while paid hours held. Measured from 2017, lathe paid hours even rose by 1,272 h. This holds whichever baseline year you use (q379, q390).
- **How labour is booked:** every role books 100% of its labour to its own work centre (q382).
- **Not an annual-grain artefact:** labour is dated on the day the operation finishes, every entry's year matches that operation's completion year, and little work was still open at the end of 2025. Comparing paid and clocked hours by year is therefore sound (q371–q373).

**What didn't:**
- **2016 is a transition year, not a fair baseline.** Clocked hours per estimated hour started 2016 near 1.0 and fell to about 0.81–0.88 by December (q374). That drop accounts for 58.5% of the 2016–2025 fall in clocked hours; lower workload accounts for the rest (q385, q391). From 2017 the split reverses, and lower workload drives it (−14,314 h).
- **The 2016 drop happened on the same work.** For identical parts, estimates per piece barely changed (1.01–1.02×) but clocked hours per piece fell to 0.76–0.86× (q389). So "clocking hasn't slipped" is only true from 2017. Whether the 2016 drop was real efficiency or labour stopped being booked to jobs, the records can't tell.
- **Laser and paint.** Their "flat workload, more paid hours" rests on 2016, when both crews were short-staffed and on overtime. From 2017, laser workload fell while paid hours rose 1,896 h, and some of that was planned: laser had two hiring requests opened because of backlog. Painter paid hours rose only 213 h, so paint no longer counts as a case of staffing added (q379, q386, q390).

**The money:**
- **The size depends on the baseline.** Against 2017 the figure is about $349,162 a year; comparing three-year averages (2017–19 vs 2023–25) it is $255,110. The finding's $405,555 comes from the 2016 baseline (q379).
- **It isn't a cost that grew.** Total paid hours moved only +511 h from 2016 to 2025 (q391); what fell was clocked work.
- **It's hard to recover directly.** Against 2017 it equals 7.92 full-time equivalents spread over 8 roles, with no role above 1.73 (q390). It becomes savings only by matching hours to workload, through attrition or cross-training, or by bringing in more work.

**Still uncertain:** what the unclocked time is spent on (there are no indirect clock codes), why lathe and inspector are above 0.69 unclocked in every year, and what caused the 2016 drop. Someone should check whether booking practice changed that year before any of it is counted as idle capacity.
